comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces risks from unauthorized gray market reselling, which can distort demand and pricing, complicate forecasting, and harm reputation if substandard or altered products fail.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose specific risks associated with unauthorized 'gray market' sales, noting that these activities distort pricing and demand dynamics, complicate demand forecasting, and introduce risks of counterfeit or substandard products. AMD explicitly states that gray market products create 'shadow inventory that is not visible to us, making it difficult to forecast demand accurately' and compete with 'heavily discounted gray market products,' which 'negatively impacts our margins.' Similarly, Intel reports that 'Gray market products can distort demand and pricing dynamics in our distribution channel' and that such activity 'can make forecasting demand more challenging.' Both companies also highlight the risk to reputation or customer satisfaction if gray market products are altered, damaged, or substandard, with AMD noting risks of 'customer satisfaction issues' and Intel stating 'our reputation may be harmed when these products fail or are found to be substandard.'

sentences.text: Gray market products result in shadow inventory that is not visible to us, making it difficult to forecast demand accurately.

Also, when gray market products enter the market, we and our distribution channels compete with these heavily discounted gray market products, which adversely affects demand for our products and negatively impacts our margins.

From time to time, our products are diverted from our authorized distribution channels and are sold on the "gray market." Our inability to control gray market activities could result in customer satisfaction issues because any time products are purchased outside our authorized distribution channels there is a risk that our customers are buying counterfeit or substandard products, including products that may have been altered, mishandled or damaged, or are used products represented as new.
Gray market activity is difficult to monitor and can make forecasting demand more challenging.
Gray market products can distort demand and pricing dynamics in our distribution channel and certain geographies, which at times adversely affects our revenue opportunities.
Gray market products also sometimes include parts that have been altered or damaged, and our reputation may be harmed when these products fail or are found to be substandard.

comparisons.peer_topic: Demand volatility from unpredictable market dynamics
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand estimates for new use cases like generative AI and DGX Cloud are difficult to predict and can create volatility, and demand for newly shipped CPU products also creates prediction volatility. Unexpected use cases such as cryptocurrency mining have impacted demand with volatile spikes and drops; while Ethereum 2.0 reduced GPU mining usage creating aftermarket sales that may hurt new GPU demand, forecasting remains difficult due to gray market reselling.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA identify gray market reselling as a specific factor that hinders accurate demand forecasting. AMD states that 'Gray market products result in shadow inventory that is not visible to us, making it difficult to forecast demand accurately.' NVIDIA similarly discloses that when products are resold online or on the unauthorized 'gray market,' it 'also makes demand forecasting difficult.' Additionally, both companies note the competitive impact of gray market goods; AMD warns that 'we and our distribution channels compete with these heavily discounted gray market products, which adversely affects demand,' while NVIDIA adds that 'Gray market products and reseller marketplaces compete with our new products and distribution channels.'

Gray market products and reseller marketplaces compete with our new products and distribution channels.
